hero.title: The history of Lishui, written one entry at a time
hero.lede: From the founding of the county in 591 CE to its reconstitution as a district in 2013; from annalistic gazetteer entries to the old bridges on the heritage list. Every entry carries its sources, marks what is uncertain, and appears in Chinese and English.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.lede: Only entries with a usable year appear here. Entries of unknown precision are listed on the list pages only and are kept off the axis.
timeline.offAxisNote: A further {n} entries have no usable date precision and are kept off the axis; they appear on the index and list pages only.

indexPage.lede: Every entry in chronological order, for a quick check of what has and has not been written. Entries without a year come last.

about.lede: Lishui History is the first sub-site of A Place Called Lishui. It covers the administrative history of Lishui District, its annals, its heritage sites, its archaeological discoveries, selections from the old gazetteers and its modern history.
about.scopeBody: Three entity types: events, places and articles. People are not given entries of their own; they are referenced from the biographical sub-site. Only published entries appear here, and nothing without a traceable source is published.
about.sourceBody: Sources are ranked: gazetteers and inscriptions; government pages and heritage lists; archaeological reports and academic papers; and site visits. Where sources disagree they are set side by side with each attributed, and no side is chosen; tradition and record are kept in separate sections, and traditions keep their original wording. Source records are catalogued in the language of the original: the publisher is given in English as well, while the rights note and the citation locator (juan, section, page) stay in the original language, so that a reader can find the passage in the source itself.
about.fixBody: If you find a factual error, a dead link or an inconsistent rendering of a proper name, open an issue in the network's repository, giving the entry ID and your evidence. Once checked, the entry is corrected and its updated field changed to that day.
about.gateBody: Every entry passes the content repository's validation script before it is stored: required fields, controlled vocabularies, resolvable sources and relations, Chinese-English pairing and consistent proper names. Events must carry a date, and a heritage site that states a protection level must also state its listing.
about.techBody: The site is static. Markdown from the content repository is rendered at build time; there is no database and no client-side framework. The timeline, the filters, the search and the list paging all run on the generated pages.

footer.about: Lishui History is one of the sub-sites of A Place Called Lishui. Entry text is licensed CC BY 4.0 and sources are recorded one by one.
